title: Quantum validity of the Zhang--Yeung inequality
source: Bao, Cao, Walter, and Wang discuss this exact unrestricted four-party candidate in Section 4.2 \sourcecite{ref:42d3-bao15}{Bao15}. The statement is rewritten here to make its hypotheses and success criterion self-contained.
progress: For classical random variables, inequality~\eqref{eq:42d3-2} is the Zhang--Yeung non-Shannon inequality. It was proved by Zhang and Yeung and later treated systematically by Dougherty, Freiling, and Zeger \sourcecite{ref:42d3-zhang98}{Zhang98}\sourcecite{ref:42d3-dfz11}{DFZ11}.

The 2025 Quantum Entropy Prover paper still identifies the search for additional unconstrained quantum entropy inequalities as open. Its Section V.A proves a related five-party inequality. Classically, an auxiliary-copy construction turns that precursor into a four-party non-Shannon inequality; the five-party quantum proof does not establish the required four-party quantum extension. \sourcecite{ref:42d3-huang25}{Huang25}

A second important distinction is between failure to derive an inequality from strong subadditivity and an actual violating density operator. A linear-programming witness outside the basic entropy cone need not be realizable by a quantum state. Likewise, the known constrained quantum inequalities, which assume specified conditional mutual informations vanish, do not settle this unconstrained question. \sourcecite{ref:42d3-huang25}{Huang25}

comment:
Retained as unresolved. Bao, Cao, Walter, and Wang provide an explicit source for the candidate, while the later entropy-cone work documents the broader gap in unconstrained quantum entropy inequalities.

Useful research target: Either prove the displayed inequality for unrestricted density operators or exhibit a finite-dimensional state with a rigorously certified negative difference between its right- and left-hand sides. Numerical minimization alone would be a search tool, not a proof of validity.
